paper_title: OpenAssistant Conversations -- Democratizing Large Language Model   Alignment
caption: Left: Relative share of the most frequent languages in the dataset. Right: Distribution of contributions among users.
model_annotation: This pie chart displays the relative share of the most frequent languages represented in a dataset, as described in the context of the OpenAssistant Conversations project. The chart contains approximately 10 distinguishable slices, each representing a different language category. The largest slice corresponds to English at 42.8%, rendered in a medium blue, followed by Spanish at 31.4% in a darker blue, making these two categories the dominant portions of the chart. Russian accounts for 5.7% in a blue shade, followed by German at 3.6%, French at 2.9%, and Chinese at 2.5%, each progressively smaller and depicted in varying lighter shades of blue. Thai represents 1.9%, Portuguese (Brazil) accounts for 1.7%, and Catalan is shown at 1.6%, all appearing as very thin slices in lighter blue tones. An "Other" category comprises 5.8% and is shown in a light or pale blue. Percentage labels are displayed either within or adjacent to each slice, and the language labels are placed outside the chart near their corresponding segments. The slices appear to be arranged roughly in descending order of size moving clockwise from the top-left, with the color palette transitioning through various shades of blue from darker to lighter tones as the slices decrease in size. No separate legend box is included; instead, labels are placed directly alongside the chart.
